text:
Washington scored 23 seconds in, led 4-1 before the second period was half over, and still needed an empty stretch of defending to hold on. The Capitals won 5-3, but the numbers say the game was a coin flip: WSH and PIT each finished with just under 4.0 expected goals, and each team deserved to win 50 percent of the time.

The first period belonged to the Capitals, who out-chanced Pittsburgh 2.41 to 0.24 in expected goals. Anthony Beauvillier opened the scoring on a backhand at 00:23, Bryan Rust tied it on a 4 percent snap shot at 1:19, and Tom Wilson put WSH back in front at 11:51. Pierre-Luc Dubois made it 3-1 early in the second, and Alex Tuch's goal at 13:14 pushed the lead to 4-1. Wilson picked up two assists and Dubois added a goal and an assist, which is how they landed the first two stars.

Then the game turned. PIT generated 2.11 expected goals in the second period to WSH's 0.99, and Tommy Novak scored at 14:05 before Nick Robertson tipped one in at 18:01 to make it 4-3. Pittsburgh kept pressing in the third, out-chancing WSH 1.62 to 0.59, but Logan Thompson (27 saves, 0.97 goals saved above expected) held the line. Ryan Leonard's power-play goal at 3:55 of the third made it 5-3. Arturs Silovs allowed 1.0 more goals than his shot quality deserved, and PIT's 21 giveaways to WSH's 11 gave the Capitals the extra margin the analytics said wasn't there.
